power: Configure power management for block devices Add udev rule that runs a script to configure APM for block devices when supported, and the standby timeout otherwise. APM level 254 (max performance) is used when running on AC, and level 1 (lowest power) when on battery. The standby timeout is 2h on AC and 5s on battery. For SanDisk SSDs power management is not configured since the implementation is too aggressive (b/35524329). BUG=chromium:741938, chromium:214886 TEST=butterfly (w/ HDD) unplug AC # wait 30s hdparm -B /dev/sda => APM_level = 1 plug AC # wait 5s hdparm -B /dev/sda => APM_level = 254 peppy (KINGSTON SNS4151) unplug AC # wait 30s hdparm -B /dev/sda => APM_level = 1 plug AC # wait 5s hdparm -B /dev/sda => APM_level = 254 falco (LITEONIT LSS-16, APM not supported) hdparm -B /dev/sda => APM_level = not supported unplug AC # wait 30s dd if=/dev/sda of=/dev/null bs=1M skip=$(expr ${RANDOM} % 10000) \ count=1 2> /dev/null && sleep 6 && hdparm -C /dev/sda => drive state is: standby (most of the times) repeat 10x plug AC # wait 5s dd if=/dev/sda of=/dev/null bs=1M skip=$(expr ${RANDOM} % 10000) \ count=1 2> /dev/null && sleep 6 && hdparm -C /dev/sda => drive state is: active/idle repeat 10x wolf (SanDisk SSD i110) unplug AC # wait 30s hdparm -B /dev/sda => APM_level = off dd if=/dev/sda of=/dev/null bs=1M skip=$(expr ${RANDOM} % 10000) \ count=1 2> /dev/null && sleep 6 && hdparm -C /dev/sda => drive state is: standby (most of the times) repeat 10x plug AC # wait 5s hdparm -B /dev/sda => APM_level = off dd if=/dev/sda of=/dev/null bs=1M skip=$(expr ${RANDOM} % 10000) \ count=1 2> /dev/null && sleep 6 && hdparm -C /dev/sda => drive state is: active/idle repeat 10x CQ-DEPEND=CL:915302 Change-Id: Iaa3939f12640116ed4d5c06a25c8c0ee0a47eeae Signed-off-by: Matthias Kaehlcke <mka@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/914537 Tested-by: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM : nl80211: check netlink protocol in socket release notification A non-privileged user can create a netlink socket with the same port_id as used by an existing open nl80211 netlink socket (e.g. as used by a hostapd process) with a different protocol number. Closing this socket will then lead to the notification going to nl80211's socket release notification handler, and possibly cause an action such as removing a virtual interface. Fix this issue by checking that the netlink protocol is NETLINK_GENERIC. Since generic netlink has no notifier chain of its own, we can't fix the problem more generically. Signed-off-by: Dmitry Ivanov <dima@ubnt.com> Signed-off-by: Johannes Berg <johannes.berg@intel.com> (cherry picked from commit 8f815cdde3e550e10c2736990d791f60c2ce43eb) BUG=b:72893611 TEST=Verified on DUT that this fixes VIF going down issue. Change-Id: I34f7efd3e5490e1a9d8309460d09ff3564949ecd Signed-off-by: Neelothpala Chaithanya <cneelothpala@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/952026 Commit-Ready: Chaithanya Neelothpala <cneelothpala@google.com> Tested-by: Chaithanya Neelothpala <cneelothpala@google.com> Reviewed-by: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@google.com> Reviewed-by: Kan Yan <kyan@google.com>

FROMLIST: drm/dp: Correctly mask DP_TRAINING_AUX_RD_INTERVAL values for DP 1.4 DP_TRAINING_AUX_RD_INTERVAL with DP 1.3 spec changed bit scheme from 8 bits to 7 bits in DPCD 0x000e. The 8th bit describes a new feature, for panels that use this new feature, this would cause a wait interval for clock recovery of at least 512 ms, much higher then spec maximum of 16 ms. This behavior is described in table 2-158 of DP 1.4 spec address 0000Eh. To avoid breaking panels that are not spec compliant we now warn on invalid values. V2: commit title/message, masking all 7 bits, warn on out of spec values.
